subject: Startups
title: Goodhart's Law in Startups
description: A short lesson to help you apply Goodhart's Law in Startups.

hook.text: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. Charles Goodhart wrote that in 1975.

buildup.text: A startup targets DAU. The team adds aggressive push notifications. DAU rises, but users hate the experience.

discovery.text: The metric improved, but the business got worse. Optimizing one number at the expense of everything else is toxic.

twist.text: Wells Fargo set aggressive account-opening targets. Employees opened millions of fake accounts to hit the number.

climax.text: The fix: use metric constellations instead of single numbers. Track the target metric alongside guardrail metrics.

punchline.text: Hitting a metric is easy. Hitting it without breaking things is hard.

quiz.question: What does Goodhart's Law warn about?
options: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being useful
Only large companies can track metrics
